decisions.reason: As a core organic line extension in a standard sliced-ham format, it fits the firm's strategy well and can be kept with low incremental cost.
This organic Kasseler variant is somewhat narrower than ham but still close to the firm's core cured-meat business, so the option value of keeping it remains positive.
Organic pepper salami is a differentiated but still familiar category that uses existing salami capabilities, making it a relatively inexpensive option to retain.
An exotic teriyaki aspic specialty for the deli counter is a niche experiment whose demand should be clear after three years, so resources are better redeployed if it has not become a clear winner.
Fennel-flavoured sliced salami is a more taste-specific niche product, and with several other adjacent meat-product options the firm is likely to prune this one if traction is only moderate.
A classic liver pâté with veal is closely aligned with the firm's premium traditional assortment and likely has low carrying costs within existing production routines.
